title: Implement backend limit checking system
description: Add complete infrastructure for checking task/project limits: constants, schema updates, helper functions, and quota query. Free users: 2 projects max, ~50 tasks max. Paid users with 'no-limits' feature: unlimited.
acceptance: Constants file with FREE_TASK_LIMIT (50) and FREE_PROJECT_LIMIT (2)
Schema updated: 'no-limits' feature added, 'no-task-limit' removed
checkTaskLimit(ctx, userAuthId) returns { current: number, max: number }
checkProjectLimit(ctx, userAuthId) returns { current: number, max: number }
getUserQuota query returns { taskCurrent, taskMax, projectCurrent, projectMax }
max == -1 for unlimited users
Uses Convex aggregates for efficient counting
All functions respect 'no-limits' feature flag
notes: This is the foundation for all limit enforcement. getUserQuota is only for account page display, not inline UI counters.

title: Enforce limits in create mutations
description: Update createTask and createProject mutations to check limits before allowing creation and throw LimitReached errors when limits are hit.
acceptance: createTask checks limit via checkTaskLimit before insert
createProject checks limit via checkProjectLimit before insert
Both throw ConvexError with type 'LimitReached' when current >= max
Error includes ctx: { current, max, resource } for UI consumption
Users with 'no-limits' feature (max = -1) bypass checks
Existing tests pass or are updated appropriately
notes: Error format: { type: 'LimitReached', msg: '[Resource] limit reached', ctx: { current, max, resource: 'tasks'|'projects' } }. Frontend catches these to show upgrade prompts.

title: Implement Stripe webhook handler
description: Create Convex HTTP endpoint to receive Stripe webhooks for payment events. Handle checkout completion (one-time and subscription) and subscription cancellation. Update user 'no-limits' feature based on payment status.
acceptance: HTTP endpoint at /api/stripe/webhook receives POST requests
Webhook signature verification using Stripe secret
Handles checkout.session.completed event: grants 'no-limits' feature
Handles customer.subscription.deleted event: revokes 'no-limits' feature
Distinguishes between one-time payment and subscription via metadata or mode
Updates users table via internal mutation
Returns 200 for successful processing, 400 for invalid signature
Logs events for debugging (can use console for now)
notes: Use Stripe SDK for signature verification. Webhook signing secret will be configured in Stripe dashboard. Consider storing Stripe customer ID on user record for future reference. For one-time payments, 'no-limits' is permanent; for subscriptions, it's active until cancelled.

title: Create upgrade/subscription page
description: Build complete upgrade page at /account/upgrade showing current tier, quota, and pricing options with Stripe payment links. Users can choose between subscription or one-time early supporter payment.
acceptance: Route exists at /account/upgrade (or /account/subscription)
Displays current tier (Free vs Supporter/Unlimited)
Shows quota via getUserQuota: 'X/Y tasks, X/Y projects'
Two pricing cards: Subscription and One-Time Early Supporter
Each card has button linking to Stripe payment link (URLs TBD/configurable)
Success state: shows confirmation when returning from Stripe (query param or state)
Upgrade page is accessible from authenticated routes
Good UX: clear benefits listed, mobile responsive
notes: Stripe payment links will be created manually in Stripe dashboard. Store URLs in environment variables or config. Success handling can be simple (check for ?success=true param or poll user features). Prices TBD - leave placeholder text.

title: Add limit counters and upgrade navigation
description: Add proactive UI elements showing remaining quota near create buttons with info icons that navigate to upgrade page. Users should always know how close they are to limits.
acceptance: Counter near 'Create Project' button: 'X/Y free projects' (or 'Unlimited' for paid)
Counter near 'Create Task' button: 'X/Y free tasks' (or 'Unlimited' for paid)
Info icons next to counters that link to /account/upgrade
Counters use checkTaskLimit/checkProjectLimit (or local equivalent)
Counters hidden or show 'Unlimited' when user has 'no-limits' feature
Counters update reactively when projects/tasks created or deleted
Good visual hierarchy: non-intrusive but visible
notes: Find 'Create Project' and 'Create Task' buttons in UI - likely in projects list page and task editor. May need to pass quota data down as props or use Convex query directly in components.

title: Add limit-reached error handling and support CTA
description: Handle LimitReached errors from backend with upgrade prompts, and add 'Support Development' button to empty tasks state.
acceptance: Catch LimitReached errors from createTask/createProject mutations
Show modal or toast with upgrade message when limit hit
Error UI includes current/max counts and CTA button to upgrade page
Good UX: clear, not annoying, easy to dismiss
'Support Development' button in empty 'today's tasks' block
Support button navigates to /account/upgrade
All navigation to upgrade page works correctly
notes: Empty tasks block likely in planner or home view. LimitReached error handling may need global error boundary or local try/catch in create actions. Consider using existing modal/toast components.

title: Stripe setup documentation and end-to-end testing
description: Document Stripe payment link creation, webhook configuration, and verify complete monetization flow works end-to-end in test mode.
acceptance: Documentation for creating Stripe payment links (subscription and one-time)
Documentation for webhook endpoint URL and secret configuration
Environment variables documented (webhook secret, payment link URLs)
Test: Free user hits task limit, sees upgrade prompt, clicks through to upgrade page
Test: Free user hits project limit (2), sees upgrade prompt
Test: Stripe test mode checkout completes, webhook grants 'no-limits' feature
Test: User with 'no-limits' can create unlimited tasks/projects
Test: Subscription cancellation webhook revokes 'no-limits' (if subscription)
All tests pass in development environment
deps: Add limit counters and upgrade navigation
Add limit-reached error handling and support CTA
notes: This is the final verification that everything works together. Use Stripe test mode and Stripe CLI for webhook testing. Document any gotchas or manual steps needed for production deployment.

title: Implement aggregate plugin for efficient counting
description: Replace .collect().length patterns with Convex aggregate plugin for efficient counting. Optimize checkTaskLimit and checkProjectLimit, and identify/optimize other counting-only queries throughout the codebase.
acceptance: @convex-dev/aggregate package installed and configured in convex.config.ts
checkTaskLimit uses aggregate.count() instead of .collect().length
checkProjectLimit uses aggregate.count() instead of .collect().length
Aggregate instances properly namespace by userAuthId and type
All existing tests pass with aggregate implementation
Other counting-only queries identified and optimized (if any exist)
No performance regressions - counts return same values as before
notes: Focus on places that only need counts, not full document retrieval. Aggregate plugin requires namespace/sortKey configuration. May need to update aggregate state when nodes are created/deleted. Check tasks.ts for other candidates (e.g., calculateProgress if it can be optimized).

title: Skill Sprint (dev-gated in-app experiment)
description: Prototype a daily "skill sprint" flow as a normal in-app feature, but gated behind the existing dev feature/route so experimental UX never reaches end users. Encapsulate UI + storage + LLM boundary so it can later be promoted out of /dev with minimal refactor.
acceptance: Skill Sprint route is accessible only behind existing dev gate (non-dev users see 404)
Encapsulation decisions documented (route location, data model, provider seam, migration path out of /dev)
A minimal end-to-end flow is defined via subtasks (goal -> plan -> daily -> feedback/progress)
notes: Implementation should live under routes/(authenticated)/dev/* and rely on devEnabled gating already used by /dev. Treat as part of app (not a separate project), but keep module boundaries tight to support later promotion to non-dev routes.

title: LLM: implement provider seam (Convex action)
description: Implement the provider seam as a Convex action that sends a caller-provided message to a selected provider/model and returns the provider response text. Support both app-owned API keys via env vars and user-supplied credentials via users.settingOverrides.llm (plaintext for closed alpha).
acceptance: Convex action exists that accepts { message, provider, model, credentialSource } and returns { text } (plus optional metadata)
At least one non-network stub provider exists so the seam works without external keys
At least one network provider is implemented using an env var API key (provider key source is explicit)
User-supplied credential source is supported via users.settingOverrides.llm (plaintext for closed alpha)
Message formatting is outside the seam (seam does not build prompts or artifacts)
notes: Credential sources: app env var keys (per-provider) vs user-provided keys stored in settingOverrides. Future: enforce entitlement rules for app-key usage (paid users) without blocking user-key usage.

title: Skills settings: configure LLM providers (per-user)
description: Add per-user settings UI under the Skills tab for choosing a default LLM provider/model and (optionally) entering user-provided API keys. Store settings in users.settingOverrides.llm.
acceptance: A Skills settings section exists for LLM configuration
User can select default provider and default model
User can enter/remove provider API keys (plaintext for closed alpha)
Settings persist via users.settingOverrides.llm and load reliably on refresh
User can choose whether to use app credentials vs user credentials when available (clear UX)
notes: Encryption is explicitly deferred to the 'Encryption for user-stored secrets (E2E vs TLE modes)' planning task.

title: LLM: dev interaction harness (provider-agnostic)
description: Add a minimal way to send text to an LLM provider seam and render the response, without committing to a single vendor. This is the first executable slice of the provider seam and should be reusable by multiple dev-gated experiments.
acceptance: User can submit input text and see model response rendered
Provider selection is explicit (dropdown or config switch)
At least one non-network stub/fake provider exists so the harness works without external keys
Adding a new provider is a contained change (no edits required outside the LLM/provider boundary)
notes: This is a dev-facing harness, not the full Skill Sprint flow. Seam returns provider text only; prompt formatting lives in the caller.

title: LLM: streaming responses
description: Add streaming support so LLM responses can render progressively for better UX, while keeping the non-streaming path as fallback.
acceptance: At least one UI surface can render streaming token/chunk updates
Provider seam supports streaming for at least one provider (stub streaming is acceptable)
Non-streaming path remains supported as a fallback
User can cancel an in-flight stream
notes: Valuable UX; implement after the non-streaming harness is stable.

title: Encryption for user-stored secrets (E2E vs TLE modes)
description: Plan how Wayfinder stores user secrets (e.g. user-provided LLM API keys) with explicit support for both end-to-end encryption (E2E) and transport+at-rest encryption (TLE). This should be fully fleshed out before it becomes a requirement for feature access.
acceptance: Encryption modes defined: E2E vs TLE, including what is protected against in each mode
Settings UX defined: users can choose E2E or TLE and can switch modes at any time
Key management defined for E2E (password/passkey lifecycle, recovery/rotation story, device changes)
Migration behavior defined when switching modes (what is re-encrypted, what is not, and how failures are handled)
Implementation follow-up tasks proposed (storage changes, UI, tests) without shipping code in this planning task
notes: Closed alpha can store secrets in plaintext temporarily, but plan must cover production path. Make it explicit in UX that TLE is theoretically less secure but avoids user maintenance of a personal passkey; allow switching modes anytime.

title: Add dev settings: debug toggle
description: Add a "Debug" toggle under the existing Dev settings umbrella so dev-only debug UI/behavior can be enabled/disabled without code changes.
acceptance: A new boolean setting exists under the Dev settings tab for debug behavior
Setting is visible only to users with the 'dev' feature (consistent with existing Dev settings gating)
Setting default is safe (off unless explicitly enabled, or clearly documented if default-on in local dev)
notes: This is a general dev control surface. Use existing settings schema patterns (settings.dev.*) and keep it semantically scoped to debugging rather than feature flags.

title: Extract day-boundary utility (planner + future journals)
description: Factor out UTC day-window logic from getTodaysTasks into a reusable helper. Skill Sprint experiment temporarily duplicates this; this task cleans it up.
acceptance: Single function returns { startMs, endMs, dayKey } for a given timestamp
Used by planner getTodaysTasks query
Configurable by user timezone + day-start hour (design TBD)
notes: Not blocking Skill Sprint; experiment duplicates UTC logic for now.
